title: Operating Lines of Credit Lendable Limit Cushion After Recent Overadvance Fees
content:
An Operating Lines of Credit line that has recently been charged overadvance fees is brought back inside its borrowing base with a cushion: the limit it is paid down to is set lower than the limit itself.

## Rule

The limit left after the reserve is taken:

- **at 0.98 of itself** when two or more overadvance fees were charged on the line in the twelve whole months before today;
- **at itself less USD 5,000** (5000) when exactly one was;
- **at itself** when none was.

The count is of fee charges with the overadvance fee code in the line's transaction history whose dates fall in the twelve whole months before today. The cushioned limit is the figure the outstanding principal is measured against when the shortfall is worked out.

## Table (hypothetical limit after the reserve of USD 1,395,500.00)

| Overadvance fees in the twelve whole months before today | Cushioned limit |
|---|---|
| None | USD 1,395,500.00 |
| Exactly one | USD 1,395,500.00 less USD 5,000.00, that is USD 1,390,500.00 |
| Two | 0.98 of USD 1,395,500.00, that is USD 1,367,590.00 |
| Three | USD 1,367,590.00 |

A lower cushioned limit means a larger shortfall: with USD 1,523,456.78 outstanding, the shortfall measured against USD 1,390,500.00 is USD 132,956.78.
